chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The Qa'im will rise, and there is no bond, nor covenant, nor allegiance upon anyone's neck.
ai.seo_question: What is the political status of Imam al-Mahdi at the time of his rise?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith highlights the political and spiritual autonomy of Imam al-Qa'im upon his reappearance, noting that no prior ruler holds a claim of allegiance (bay'ah) or covenant ('ahd) over him. This signifies a complete break from the legitimacy of previous caliphates and establishes his rule as divinely ordained rather than derived from human succession. It underscores the concept of *al-Intizar* (awaiting) as a period of preparing for a fresh, independent Islamic governance.
